title: Evoked responses to elevated sounds
description: This dataset comprises EEG recordings from two experiments investigating evoked responses to sounds presented at varying elevations from loudspeakers in a hemi-anechoic chamber. In Experiment I, a deviant detection paradigm was used to examine responses to changes in sound source elevation between an adapter and probe stimulus. In Experiment II, a one-back task assessed elevation discrimination via white noise adaptation and localization judgments, including a subset of subjects tested with sound localization disrupted by ear molds. The dataset also includes behavioral localization test data for most subjects.
methods_description: Subjects were presented with bursts of pink or white noise from loudspeakers positioned at various elevations within a hemi-anechoic chamber. In Experiment I (deviant detection), subjects heard an adapter sound followed by a probe sound, with EEG and behavioral responses (button presses to deviants) recorded. In Experiment II (one-back task), subjects heard white noise through open headphones followed by a burst from a loudspeaker at a specific elevation, with target trials requiring localization judgments. A subset of subjects in Experiment II completed a second session with ear molds disrupting elevation perception.
